subject: Dedicated reservation options & phased ramp — AuroraEdge
messages:
From: Aaron Mills <aaron@auroraedge.com>
To: soojin_lee@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 3 Aug 2026 07:22:00 -0700
Subject: Redwood dedicated — baseline sizing and ramp options

Soojin — thanks again for the demo last week. We ran the internal sizing exercise and want to get concrete about committed capacity versus burst needs. High level: production traffic will start small (10 TPS equivalent), spike to 60 TPS on inference-heavy days, and long-term steady-state expected ~25 TPS. Latency requirement is 95th <= 300ms for production-critical endpoints.

Attached is a short requirement sheet (auroraedge_requirements.pdf). Can you provide 1) a small/medium/large reserved proposal with minimum guaranteed GPUs, 2) a recommended ramp schedule over the first 12 months, and 3) options for short-term burst (hot lanes or burst credits) plus any pricing guardrails? We need a proposal to circulate in our procurement review by Aug 10.

Appreciate quick options.

— Aaron
VP of Infrastructure, AuroraEdge

[Attachment: auroraedge_requirements.pdf]

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Aaron Mills <aaron@auroraedge.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 3 Aug 2026 11:03:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Redwood dedicated — baseline sizing and ramp options

Aaron — thanks for the clear brief and the attachment. Drafting three concise reservation structures below. I'll attach a one-page proposal (redwood_dedicated_proposal_v1.pdf) and a draft SOW for your legal team. Quick summary up front, then we can iterate.

Options (baseline GPU = A100-style equivalent):

1) Lean Start (pilot-friendly) — Minimum guarantee: 8 GPUs
   - Typical throughput: fits early 10 TPS, burst to ~30 TPS with transient queueing
   - Ramp: 8 GPUs month 0–3, add 8 GPUs month 4, evaluate at month 6 for next tranche
   - Burst: burst credits pool (50 GPU-hours/month) for spikes; host fallback to shared hosts if exhausted
   - Pricing: lower commitment discount, per-hour overage at 1.4x list

2) Balanced Growth (recommended for predictable latency) — Minimum guarantee: 20 GPUs
   - Typical throughput: steady-state 25 TPS, headroom for 60 TPS with short bursts
   - Ramp: 10 GPUs month 0 (warm start), 20 GPUs month 2, 20–40 GPUs month 6 based on metrics
   - Burst: hot lanes (dedicated preemptible warm pool) for sustained peak handling; auto-scale policy available
   - Pricing: mid-tier commitment with windowed smoothing credits; SLA tier 99.9%

3) Anchored Throughput (enterprise reserve) — Minimum guarantee: 48 GPUs
   - Typical throughput: comfortably supports 60 TPS with consistent <300ms 95th
   - Ramp: 24 GPUs month 0, 48 GPUs month 2, add 24 GPUs month 9 if usage warrants
   - Burst: guaranteed burst windows and higher burst credits; dedicated standby for predictability
   - Pricing: highest upfront discount, custom SLA, included warm-up credits

Key tradeoffs and notes:
- Warm-start vs. cold activation: warm lanes reduce latency but consume baseline capacity; pilot option minimizes cost but incurs transient tail latency during spikes.
- We recommend starting with the Balanced Growth option if AuroraEdge prioritizes latency predictability and cost control.
- We can tailor ramp cadence to your procurement cycle and add an auto-fallback to Redwood Hosted API during extreme capacity events.

Next steps: I attached the proposal and SOW. If we agree on a baseline option, I'll pull recommended pricing and a draft term sheet and loop pricing ops (Ben) for discount approvals. Can you confirm target contract length (12 vs 24 months) and whether AuroraEdge needs on-prem edge nodes in month 1?

Best —
Soojin Lee
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood_dedicated_proposal_v1.pdf]

Pricing ops guidance (high level):
- If AuroraEdge signs 24 months commit, we can offer: Balanced Growth at 20 GPUs with 18% commitment discount + 200 GPU-hours/month burst credits; standard SLA 99.9%.
- For 12 months, offer 14% discount + 100 GPU-hours/month burst credits.
- Minimums: we should avoid sub-6 GPU guarantees for production workloads with 300ms targets; 8 GPUs is OK strictly for pilot only.
- Ramp recommendation for commercial terms: structured tranches tied to usage milestones (X% of token volume or sustained TPS for 7 consecutive days). Suggested tranche triggers: 10k reqs/day => +8 GPUs; 40k reqs/day => +16 GPUs.

Commercial levers to negotiate:
- Warm-up credits (one-time GPU-hour credit) to help with model warming during first 30 days.
- Burst window caps and overage pricing caps for first 3 months.
- Optional early-exit clause at month 9 with a defined wind-down fee for pilot customers.

I'll draft a pricing sheet and term summary after Soojin confirms AuroraEdge preference and contract length. Marissa — can you prep the SOW version that includes the tranche triggers and warm-up credits?

— Ben
